claims.subject: e-pure-food-act
claims.text: President Theodore Roosevelt signed the Pure Food and Drugs Act into law on 30 June 1906.

sources.note: Says the House approved the conference report on 29 June and that the President signed the law the next day.
Says Congress passed the original Pure Food and Drugs Act in 1906 and that President Roosevelt signed it; no day.
Lists the Pure Food and Drugs Act among the 1906 milestones of US food and drug law; no day.

claims.subject: e-haber-prize
claims.text: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry for 1918, presented to Fritz Haber in 1919, honoured his synthesis of ammonia from its elements, the basis of mass-produced agricultural fertiliser.

sources.note: Gives the prize motivation as the synthesis of ammonia from its elements and says Haber received the prize a year later, in 1919.
Says the synthesis earned Haber the 1918 prize and enabled mass production of agricultural fertilisers.
Hosts the Nobel lecture titled The Synthesis of Ammonia from Its Elements.

claims.subject: e-borlaug-prize
claims.text: Norman Borlaug, whose wheat breeding is tied to the Green Revolution, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

sources.note: Lists Norman Borlaug as the laureate of the Nobel Peace Prize 1970.
States that the Nobel Peace Prize 1970 was awarded to Norman Borlaug.
Calls Borlaug the 1970 Nobel Prize winner and father of the Green Revolution; it does not describe the wheat work.
